facet_evidence.comparison: measured by scripts/check-comparison.mjs, which prices all four D-01 paths through the real sizing engine on a committed offline weather profile and then audits that they are comparable. One owner (assets/js/sizing/paths.js) prices turnkey, lease, selfpurchase and diy for ONE sized system over ONE 20-year horizon with ONE set of definitions; the comparability audit (scripts/lib/paths-integrity.mjs) is a build assertion kept off the wire. The installer's all-in price is no longer a multiplier: the 10x-cheapest / 5x-dearest estimator and the flat $1,500-$3,000 hookup are deleted, so the gap on the page is a gap between two registry prices rather than between two counting rules. Walked on the probe site (US/ppa) selfpurchase $12,341 < turnkey $20,919 < lease $26,131, incentives applied to the owner only; the cheapest route varies by market (selfpurchase in US/DE/AU/BR, diy in IN), and D-10 legality removes the diy card in US (licensed electrical work required), DE (mounting restricted) and BR (unverified jurisdiction) rather than offering it quietly. Every adjacent gap reconstructs additively from its components (year0, incentives, O&M, replacements, lease payments); hardware wears out on a clock not on who paid, so turnkey/selfpurchase/diy share one replacement schedule and the lease carries none; a lease's end-of-term buyout sits inside its own 20-year figure and a PPA still running at the horizon says so. No-tariff, no-system and unverified-jurisdiction each refuse with a stated reason, and the four premium/break-even figures are differences between model prices. Mutated spends, horizons, bill cuts, ranges and rankings are each caught by the audit.
facet_evidence.usecases: measured by scripts/check-usecases.mjs, which walks all six through the real engine on a committed offline weather profile. One registry (assets/js/sizing/usecases.js) owns each case's inputs, its own outcome metric and its own verdict; the legacy systemGoal x hardwareConfig pair is derived from it and hidden. Six distinct metrics, no sharing: billcut bill_cut_pct 80.1% works; tou tou_peak_offset_pct 18.4% not-here (18.4% of peak energy = $123 over 20y against a $748 bank); backup outage_coverage_pct 100% works, sized on the ticked essentials not the home; reserve reserve_tradeoff not-here (the cheapest 80% cut carries no battery, so there is nothing to reserve in); offgrid grid_independence_pct 99.33% partial (59 unmet h worst year); portable portable_runtime_coverage_pct 0.27% not-here (200 W panel cannot sustain 2.4 kWh/day; shore power takes it to 100%). 4 of 6 decline on the probe site. Added R-UC-03/04/06 (outage simulator with measured start SOC, reserve floor, portable day model). F-13/F-14/F-16 closed.
facet_evidence.privacy: FALLBACK line only: when jev-results-privacy-browser is present the judge reads the line composed from that run instead and this text is not consulted. check-privacy.mjs statically proves all six clauses: 0 cookies; no identifier stored or logged; coordinates rounded to 0.01 deg on the device before any egress (one helper, asserted for every outbound URL builder); no ad, tracker, affiliate link or lead capture; advisor egress disclosed on the page; nothing collected the visitor did not choose to send. Its runtime half, check-privacy-browser.mjs, measures the same claims in a real browser, because an HttpOnly cookie, a request from injected markup and storage written by a worker are each invisible to a source scan. Egress the browser half measures is nominatim.openstreetmap.org and open.er-api.com, both declared in connect-src.
